page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-aligned virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 1 physical CPU core with simultaneous multithreading, presenting 2 dedicated vCPUs to the hypervisor. The system is provisioned with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Local storage is not included.

Performance metrics highlight strong single-threaded capabilities alongside expected multi-core scaling limitations. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance ranks in the top tier, complemented by strong single-core Geekbench scores. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks like stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU overall scores fall in the bottom quarter due to the 2 vCPU limit. Memory read and write uncached bandwidth sit in the middle tier at 47.32 GB/sec and 27.49 GB/sec respectively, while PassMark database operations perform in the bottom ten percent.

From a resource design perspective, the 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers a compute-dense configuration for low-footprint operations without paying for unused memory overhead. Tradeoffs include limited concurrency and weak database operation throughput, ruling out heavy database software or multi-threaded build tasks. Appropriate workload fits include lightweight single-threaded microservices, basic API routing, and single-threaded batch processing jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-focused virtual server equipped with a 2-vCPU dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it features 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a 3 Gbps network baseline, with no local SSD storage. Benchmark evaluation shows top-tier single-core CPU execution alongside strong single-threaded Geekbench scores, but overall multi-core performance and PassMark database operations remain in lower performance brackets due to hardware core limits. Uncached memory bandwidth sits at moderate levels. With a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation, this instance provides cost efficiency for low-concurrency single-threaded utilities, basic API endpoints, and light background tasks where high memory capacity is not required.
